content: In anatomy, a fissure refers to a groove, natural division, deep furrow, cleft, or tear in various parts of the body. Below are specific types of fissures, categorized as natural or abnormal: Natural Fissures: 1. Auricular fissure: This is located in the temporal bone. 2. Fissure of Bichat: Found beneath the corpus callosum in the cerebellum of the brain. 3. Broca's fissure: Located in the third left frontal fold of the brain. 4. Burdach's fissure: Connects the brain's insula to the inner surface of the operculum. 5. Calcarine fissure: Extends from the occipital region of the cerebrum to the occipital fissure. 6. Callosomarginal fissure: Found on the mesial surface of the cerebrum. 7. Central fissure (or Ronaldo's fissure): Separates the frontal and parietal lobes of the brain. 8. Clevenger's fissure: Found in the inferior temporal lobe of the brain. 9. Collateral fissure: Located on the inferior surface of the cerebrum. 10. Fissure vent: Refers to a volcanic vent that does not involve explosive activity. 11. Henle's fissure: Represents the connective tissue between the muscle fibers of the heart. 12. Hippocampal fissure: Extends from the brain's corpus callosum to the tip of the temporal lobe. 13. Horizontal fissure (or Transverse fissure): Found between the cerebrum and cerebellum. It is also present in the liver and lungs. 14. Longitudinal fissure: Found on the lower surface of the liver and also separates the right and left hemispheres of the cerebrum. 15. Occipitoparietal fissure: Located between the occipital and parietal lobes of the brain. 16. Palpebral fissure: Separates the upper and lower eyelids. 17. Portal fissure: Found on the undersurface of the liver. 18. Sphenoidal fissure: Separates the wings and body of the sphenoid bone. 19. Fissure of Sylvius: Separates the frontal and parietal lobes of the brain from the temporal lobe. 20. Umbilical fissure: Found in the anterior region of the liver. 21. Wernicke's fissure: Separates the temporal and parietal lobes of the brain from the occipital lobe. 22. Zygal fissure: Found in the cerebrum. Abnormal Fissures: A fissure can also refer to an unnatural tract or ulcer, most commonly found in the anus. One of the most prevalent types of abnormal fissures is the anal fissure, which is a tear in the lining of the anal canal.
